findings.title: PWA manifest ships only an SVG icon and is duplicated across three sources
evidence: apps/web/app/manifest.ts:12-18 — the only icon is /favicon.svg with sizes:"any", type image/svg+xml; no 192x192/512x512 PNG and no maskable icon
apps/web/public/manifest.json and apps/web/public/manifest.webmanifest — duplicate manifests; `diff` shows they differ only by a trailing newline
apps/web/app/layout.tsx:26 — metadata.manifest points at /manifest.webmanifest while app/manifest.ts already generates that URL, so two of the three sources are redundant/ambiguous
apps/web/public — `file apps/web/public/favicon.ico` reports SVG content (mislabeled), and no PNG/maskable/apple-touch icon exists (git ls-files)
Chromium installability requires a 192px and a 512px manifest icon (MDN "Making PWAs installable"); the SVG-only manifest does not meet it
git diff --stat 9c0b88c 8d299b8d -- apps/web/app/manifest.ts apps/web/public/ apps/web/app/layout.tsx — empty; unchanged since the previous run
findings.impact: Chromium browsers do not meet installability criteria (no 192/512 icon), iOS has no apple-touch-icon, and three manifest sources can drift with no single source of truth for what /manifest.webmanifest serves.
findings.recommendation: Keep one manifest source (the Next metadata route), add 192x192 + 512x512 PNG icons plus a maskable icon and a 180x180 apple-touch-icon, delete apps/web/public/manifest.json and manifest.webmanifest, and keep layout.tsx icon/manifest metadata in sync.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: apps/web/app/manifest.ts:12-18 still declares only favicon.svg; both public manifests still present and content-identical; no PNG/maskable/apple icons in apps/web/public; git diff 9c0b88c..8d299b8d shows these files unchanged. Previous status open -> still-open (never fixed). Stronger impact recorded this run: the manifest fails Chromium installability (192/512 icon requirement).

findings.title: Service worker apps/web/public/sw.js is never registered, so PWA/offline support is inert
evidence: apps/web/public/sw.js:1-53 — complete service worker (precache of 8 routes, activate cache cleanup, network-first fetch handler)
repo-wide grep for serviceWorker / navigator.serviceWorker.register / workbox in apps/** and packages/** — no matches
git log --all --oneline -S "navigator.serviceWorker" -- apps/web — empty output: no registration ever existed in history
git log --oneline -1 -- apps/web/public/sw.js — added in f02ec685 (2026-07-30, 'audit remediation'); git cat-file -e confirms it existed at 6286137 and 9c0b88c
docs/GAP_ANALYSIS.md:67 lists 'PWA / offline support — Service worker, push notifications' as not started, which contradicts the shipped sw.js
findings.impact: No offline capability, no service-worker update flow, and no install/offline behaviour; the dead file misleads maintainers and auditors into believing PWA support exists.
findings.recommendation: Either delete apps/web/public/sw.js and record the product decision, or implement registration (e.g. a small client component in the root layout) together with the safe cache design in the companion finding.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d (INV flagged sw.js). Also corrects the prior NOTIF audit evidence ('no service worker in apps/web', docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261002-0344-develop-6286137/30_notification_email_push_delivery_audit.md:87): the file has existed since f02ec685 and was present at 6286137/9c0b88c — it is simply unregistered. NOTIF-P2-001 (no Web Push) remains correct and is owned by the notifications domain; only its service-worker evidence was wrong.

findings.title: sw.js cache strategy would persist authenticated API responses and all GET 200s if registered as-is
evidence: apps/web/public/sw.js:33-53 — every same-origin GET is fetched and, when status is 200, written to cache mct-cache-v1 with no allowlist and no Cache-Control / no-store check
apps/web/next.config.mjs:23-31 — /api/v1/:path* is proxied same-origin, so authenticated API GETs are inside the SW scope
apps/web/public/sw.js:47-50 — offline fallback is `new Response("Offline", {status: 503})`, not an HTML offline page
grep for caches.delete outside the activate handler — none: no logout/session purge of cached user data
apps/web/public/sw.js:1 — cache name is a manual constant (mct-cache-v1); no build-versioned invalidation
findings.impact: If the SW is ever registered without changes, tenant/user JSON and rendered portal HTML persist in Cache Storage indefinitely (the Cache API ignores private/no-store) and can be served by the network-first fallback on a shared or lost device, outliving logout.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the fetch handler to allowlist static assets only, bypass /api/ and non-GET requests, respect no-store, precache an offline HTML route, purge user-scoped caches on logout, and serve /sw.js with Cache-Control: no-cache so updates propagate.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; satisfies the domain prompt's 'service worker cache risks' special check. Latent today because the SW is unregistered (see previous finding), but it is the blocking design issue for any registration.

findings.title: No mobile-viewport E2E or accessibility coverage (Desktop Chrome only)
evidence: apps/web/playwright.config.ts:28-40 — projects are only 'setup' and 'chromium' using devices["Desktop Chrome"]; no mobile device project
apps/web/e2e/a11y.spec.ts:84-104 — axe scan runs without setViewportSize or device emulation, so the 25-route WCAG 2.2 AA gate is desktop-geometry only
.github/workflows/e2e.yml — 'Install Playwright browsers' runs `playwright install chromium` only
docs/WEB_UI_CONVENTIONS.md:85-93 — documents the 25-route desktop gate; no viewport/mobile note
findings.impact: Mobile layout, touch-target, overflow and modal-scroll regressions cannot be caught in CI; every finding below shipped without a failing check.
findings.recommendation: Add Pixel 7 / iPhone 13 Playwright projects, run a representative a11y subset at 360x800, and assert document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= viewport width on key routes.

findings.title: About 41% of form controls render below 16px and trigger iOS Safari focus zoom
evidence: Python scan of 382 <input>/<select>/<textarea> elements in apps/web: 129 with text-sm (14px), 28 with text-xs (12px), 174 cyber-input, 51 unspecified
apps/web/components/store/QuoteBuilderClient.tsx:303,319,335,351 — quote-funnel inputs use text-sm
apps/web/components/store/IntakeFormRenderer.tsx:157-158 — intake widget inputs use text-sm
packages/ui/src/styles.css:60-66 — .cyber-input sets no font-size, so it inherits 16px while the ad-hoc inputs do not
findings.impact: iOS Safari auto-zooms the viewport when a focused control's font-size is below 16px, disrupting the public quote and intake funnels (the primary lead-capture paths) on phones.
findings.recommendation: Set a 16px mobile floor: .cyber-input { @apply text-base sm:text-sm; } and use the same text-base sm:text-sm pattern for ad-hoc inputs and selects.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Counts are from a read-only script over the 8d299b8d tree; the iOS zoom behaviour is documented Safari behaviour.

findings.title: Several modal dialogs have no max-height or vertical scroll and clip on small screens
evidence: packages/ui/src/components/Dialog.tsx:104-119 — centered panel with overflow-hidden and no max-h/overflow-y; body scroll is locked while open
apps/web/components/portal/SupportCenterClient.tsx:216-224 — create-support-ticket modal with no max-height or scroll container
apps/web/components/admin/AdminDocumentsCenterClient.tsx:1769-1779 — create-document modal (max-w-3xl) with no max-height or scroll container
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/store/promotions/PromoForm.tsx:59-69 and apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/store/categories/CategoryForm.tsx:51-61 — centered modals with no scroll

Counter-examples showing the intended pattern: apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/store/products/ProductForm.tsx:85 (max-h-[90vh] overflow-y-auto) and apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/projects/AdminProjectsClient.tsx:304-312 (container overflow-y-auto + items-start on mobile)
findings.impact: On phones, long forms can extend past the viewport with scrolling unavailable, making the submit action unreachable for document creation, support tickets, promotions and categories.
findings.recommendation: Adopt one scroll-safe modal shell (max-h-[90vh] overflow-y-auto, items-start on mobile, sticky action row) in the shared Dialog component and migrate the ad-hoc modals.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Confidence medium: no browser was run, so content height vs viewport was not rendered; the missing max-height/scroll classes are directly evidenced.

findings.title: Icon-only controls have touch targets well below the 44x44 recommendation
evidence: apps/web/components/marketing/MarketingHeader.tsx:92-106 — mobile hamburger has no padding: three h-0.5 w-7 bars, about 28x16px
apps/web/components/layout/SidebarShell.tsx:116-130 — drawer close button p-1 + h-5 icon, about 28x28px
apps/web/components/store/StoreLayoutShell.tsx:67-80 — drawer close button, about 28x28px
packages/ui/src/components/Dialog.tsx:121-128 — close button p-1.5 + h-5 icon, about 28x28px
apps/web/components/ui/ToastProvider.tsx:60-67 and apps/web/components/store/StickyMobileCta.tsx:55-64 — dismiss buttons p-1 + h-4 icon, about 24x24px
apps/web/components/portal/ProjectCalendarView.tsx:106-117 — month prev/next arrows p-1, about 24x24px
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/store/products/ProductForm.tsx:91-97 — close button with no padding, about 20x20px
apps/web/components/NotificationBell.tsx:226-231 — 'Mark all read' text-xs control, about 16px tall
findings.impact: Icon-only controls are hard to hit one-handed on phones; some are at or below the WCAG 2.5.8 24px minimum and all are below the 44px iOS / 48px Android guidance.
findings.recommendation: Give icon buttons min-h-11 min-w-11 (44px) hit areas while keeping glyph sizes, and add padding to the marketing hamburger and ProductForm close button.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Sizes are computed from Tailwind classes (rem-based), not rendered; the desktop-only a11y gate cannot detect mobile-geometry target-size issues.

findings.title: Notification dropdown is a fixed 320px panel anchored right-0 and clips on narrow phones
evidence: apps/web/components/NotificationBell.tsx:221-222 — dropdown uses absolute right-0 w-80 (320px)
apps/web/app/(portal)/layout.tsx:193-205 — the bell sits left of PortalHeaderActions (Admin Portal / Sign Out), so its right edge is inset from the viewport edge
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/layout.tsx:156-163 — same ordering in the admin header
findings.impact: On 320-375px wide phones the dropdown's left portion extends past the viewport edge, so part of the notification list is unreachable.
findings.recommendation: On small screens anchor the panel to the viewport (fixed inset-x-2 top-16 w-auto) or use w-[min(20rem,calc(100vw-2rem))].
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Confidence medium: geometry inferred from fixed widths and header ordering; not rendered.

findings.title: themeColor is declared in the deprecated metadata export, so the theme-color meta tag is not emitted
evidence: apps/web/app/layout.tsx:27 — themeColor: "#059669" is inside `metadata`

Next.js v15.5.27 packages/next/src/lib/metadata/resolve-metadata.ts — the themeColor case only adds an 'Unsupported metadata themeColor ... move it to viewport export' warning and does not set the resolved value (source fetched for the pinned version)
grep for a `viewport` export across apps/web/app — none; the framework default viewport applies
apps/web/app/manifest.ts:11 — theme_color exists only for the manifest
findings.impact: The brand colour never reaches <meta name="theme-color">, so mobile browser/OS chrome does not match the brand, and the build emits a deprecation warning.
findings.recommendation: Add `export const viewport: Viewport = { themeColor: "#059669" };` to apps/web/app/layout.tsx and remove themeColor from metadata.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Verified against the pinned Next.js 15.5.27 source (pnpm-lock.yaml: next@15.5.27).

findings.title: favicon.ico contains SVG bytes and no apple-touch-icon is declared
evidence: `file apps/web/public/favicon.ico` -> 'SVG Scalable Vector Graphics image'; `diff favicon.ico favicon.svg` is empty (byte-identical, 435 bytes each)
apps/web/app/layout.tsx:23-25 — only icon: "/favicon.svg" is declared; no apple touch icon
git ls-files apps/web/public — no PNG icon assets
findings.impact: Clients that require a real ICO/PNG may not render the icon, and iOS 'Add to Home Screen' has no proper icon (falls back to a screenshot/blank).
findings.recommendation: Ship a real multi-size .ico (or remove it) and add a 180x180 apple-touch-icon PNG; declare icons.apple in layout metadata.

report:
# Mobile, PWA, and Responsive Access Audit

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: repo-deep-dive
- Run: mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8
- Repository: MaineCyberTech/mainecybertech (read-only copy at `/tmp/opencode/mct-audit-target`)
- Branch: main
- Commit SHA: `8d299b8dc271c410b9ae2ceeda3d2c6c997af8fd`
- Generated at: 2026-10-11
- Auditor: domain subagent (MOB), static read-only analysis
- Area code: MOB
- Output path: `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8/17_mobile_pwa_responsive_access.md`
- Scope limitations: no browser was launched, no device emulation, no build, no `pnpm install`; everything below is source/config/test evidence at `8d299b8d`. Rendering-dependent conclusions (clipping, zoom, overlap) are marked with confidence. Previous-run register re-checked for Area `MOB` (one row) plus the service-worker aspect of `NOTIF-P2-001`.

## Scope

Reviewed: viewport/meta handling, responsive layout utilities, mobile navigation (marketing/portal/admin/store), touch targets, mobile forms, dialogs/tables, auth/dashboard/admin mobile headers, PWA manifest, service worker, offline fallback, install prompt, push, icons, cache strategy, update flow, background sync, mobile E2E and touch accessibility.

Not reviewed: native app wrappers (none exist), iOS/Android store packaging (none), real-device rendering, network-throttled offline behaviour, and the notification delivery backend (owned by `NOTIF`, see `30_notification_email_push_delivery_audit`).

## Evidence Reviewed

| Evidence | Type | Why relevant | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/app/layout.tsx:19-28` | Config | Root metadata: icons, manifest, themeColor | No `viewport` export |
| `apps/web/app/manifest.ts:1-20` | PWA | The generated manifest (SVG-only icon) | Added by 62de9c1b |
| `apps/web/public/manifest.json`, `apps/web/public/manifest.webmanifest` | PWA | Duplicate static manifests | Content identical (trailing newline only) |
| `apps/web/public/sw.js:1-53` | PWA | Service worker source | Never registered |
| `apps/web/public/favicon.svg`, `favicon.ico` | Icons | App icons | `.ico` contains SVG bytes |

## Verification Performed

All commands read-only against `/tmp/opencode/mct-audit-target` at `8d299b8d`.

| `git log --all --oneline -S "navigator.serviceWorker" -- apps/web` | Command | History check | **Empty** — no registration ever existed |

| Python scan of 382 `<input>/<select>/<textarea>` tags | Command | Font-size/zoom risk | 174 `cyber-input`, 129 `text-sm`, 28 `text-xs`, 51 unspecified |
| `grep -rn "<table" apps/web` (24 matches) + wrapper spot-checks | Command | Table overflow | All 24 are inside `overflow-x-auto`, or `hidden md:block` with mobile cards |
| `grep -roh "sm:\|md:\|lg:\|xl:" apps/web` | Command | Responsive coverage | 683 breakpoint utilities (sm 364, md 150, lg 128, xl 41) |
| `grep -rn "beforeinstallprompt\|pushManager\|vapid\|showNotification" apps packages` | Command | Install prompt / push | No matches |

| MDN "Making PWAs installable" | External | Installability criteria | Chromium requires 192px **and** 512px manifest icons; SW not required |

## Executive Summary

The web app is **mobile-shaped but not mobile-verified**. Responsive implementation is broad and deliberate: 683 Tailwind breakpoint utilities, three mobile drawers (portal/admin/store) with focus traps and Escape handling, mobile card fallbacks for data tables, a mobile-only sticky CTA, a skip link, and live-region announcements. All 24 `<table>`s sit inside horizontal-scroll wrappers or are replaced by cards below `md`.

The PWA story is the weak half. The manifest declares a single SVG icon and does not meet Chromium's installability criteria (192px + 512px icons required), no `apple-touch-icon` exists, and `apps/web/public/favicon.ico` contains SVG bytes. A service worker file exists but is **never registered** anywhere in the repo, so offline support, install prompt, and update flow are all inert; if it were registered as written, its fetch handler would cache every same-origin GET 200 — including authenticated `/api/v1/*` responses proxied through the web app — in persistent Cache Storage with no allowlist, no `Cache-Control` respect, and no logout purge.

Two mobile UX defects are systemic: ~41% of form controls render below 16px and will trigger iOS Safari focus zoom, and several modal dialogs have no max-height or vertical scroll, so long forms can be unreachable on a phone. No mobile-viewport E2E or a11y coverage exists (Desktop Chrome only), which is why none of this is caught by CI.

Next actions: (1) decide the PWA scope — either delete `sw.js` + duplicate manifests or implement a safe SW (static allowlist, API bypass, offline page, update flow); (2) add a 16px mobile input floor; (3) adopt one scroll-safe modal shell; (4) add a mobile Playwright project + viewport a11y scan.

## Inventory

| Item | Path / symbol | Purpose | Current state | Risk | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Responsive utilities | `packages/ui/src/styles.css:22-160`, app components | Layout scaling | Broad (683 breakpoints) | Low | `cyber-container`, `cyber-main`, grids |
| Marketing nav | `apps/web/components/marketing/MarketingHeader.tsx` | Public mobile nav | Implemented | Medium | 28×16px hamburger; no focus trap |
| Portal/admin nav | `SidebarShell.tsx` + `Portal/AdminSidebarContent` | Drawer + desktop sidebar | Implemented | Low | Focus trap, Escape, popstate close |

## Domain Scorecard

| Category | Score | Evidence | Gap | Recommended action |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Viewport | 3 | No override; Next default `width=device-width, initial-scale=1`; `global-error.tsx:26` explicit | No explicit `viewport` export; themeColor ignored | `export const viewport = { themeColor: "#059669" }` |
| Responsive layouts | 4 | 683 breakpoint utilities; drawers; mobile cards; sticky CTA | No automated mobile proof | Add mobile Playwright project |
| Mobile nav | 4 | 3 drawers with focus traps (`SidebarShell`, `StoreLayoutShell`, `MarketingHeader`) | Small close/hamburger targets; marketing menu lacks trap | Enlarge hit areas; reuse `useFocusTrap` |
| Touch targets | 2 | 9 controls measured 20–36px (see finding) | No 44px policy; no mobile target-size test | Add min 44px hit areas + test |
| Mobile forms | 2 | 129 `text-sm` + 28 `text-xs` controls of 382 | iOS focus zoom on public funnels | 16px mobile input floor |
| Mobile dialogs/tables | 3 | All tables scroll or card-ify; `ProductForm` scroll-safe | `SupportCenterClient`, doc-center create, `PromoForm`, `CategoryForm` clip | One scroll-safe modal shell |
| Auth/dashboard/admin mobile | 3 | Responsive login/MFA; wrapping headers; drawer nav | Notification dropdown clips ≤375px; admin header density | Mobile-position the dropdown; test 320–375px |
| PWA manifest | 2 | `manifest.ts` valid JSON, name/short_name/display/start_url | SVG-only icon; 3 sources; fails installability | One source + 192/512/maskable icons |
| Service worker | 1 | `sw.js` present | Never registered; unsafe cache strategy | Delete or fix + register |
| Offline fallback | 1 | `sw.js:47-50` plain-text 503 | No offline page; no registration | Offline HTML route + precache |
| Install prompt | 0 | No `beforeinstallprompt` handler anywhere | Cannot install | Add install affordance after manifest fix |
| Push notifications | 0 | No VAPID/pushManager/`showNotification` | No OS-level alerts | Owned by `NOTIF-P2-001` |

## Detailed Review

### Item: Viewport and theme colour

- Evidence: `apps/web/app/layout.tsx:19-28`; `apps/web/app/global-error.tsx:24-27`.
- What it does: relies on the Next.js default viewport meta; declares `themeColor` inside `metadata`.
- How it appears to work: Next.js 15.5.27 emits the default `width=device-width, initial-scale=1`; `metadata.themeColor` hits the "Unsupported metadata" switch case and is dropped with a build warning (source-verified).
- Current controls: framework default; explicit viewport only in the standalone error document.
- Missing controls: explicit `viewport` export; theme-color meta; `viewportFit: "cover"`/safe-area handling.
- Risks: browser chrome colour mismatch; build warning noise.
- Recommended improvement: `export const viewport: Viewport = { themeColor: "#059669" };` in `layout.tsx`.
- Suggested tests: snapshot the rendered `<head>` for `meta[name=theme-color]` and `meta[name=viewport]`.
- Suggested docs: `docs/WEB_UI_CONVENTIONS.md` "Mobile & viewport".

### Item: Responsive layouts and navigation

- Evidence: `packages/ui/src/styles.css:22-160`; `SidebarShell.tsx:70-151`; `StoreLayoutShell.tsx:27-99`; `MarketingHeader.tsx:74-146`; `cyber-container`/`cyber-main`.
- What it does: fluid containers, `sm/md/lg` grids, `lg` sidebar ↔ drawer switch, sticky mobile CTA, scrollable subnavs (`AdminSubnav.tsx:35-36`, `PortalSubnav.tsx:34-35`).
- How it appears to work: Tailwind default breakpoints; drawer uses `lg:hidden` + fixed aside.
- Current controls: focus trap, `aria-modal`, Escape, focus restore, popstate close.

### Finding ID: MOB-P2-002 (provisional) - sw.js cache strategy would persist authenticated API responses and all GET 200s if registered as-is

- Severity: P2
- Confidence: High (code); Medium (impact — SW is inert today)
- Area: MOB
- Evidence:
  - `apps/web/public/sw.js:33-53` — every same-origin GET is fetched and, on status 200, written to `mct-cache-v1` with no allowlist and no `Cache-Control`/`no-store` check
  - `apps/web/next.config.mjs:23-31` — `/api/v1/:path*` is proxied same-origin, so API GETs are in scope
  - `apps/web/public/sw.js:47-50` — offline fallback is `new Response("Offline", {status:503})`, not an HTML page
  - no logout cache purge (grep: no `caches.delete` outside `activate`)
- What is happening: the Cache API ignores `private`/`no-store`, so tenant/user JSON and rendered portal HTML would persist indefinitely in Cache Storage and be served by the network-first fallback.
- Why it matters: on a shared or lost device, cached authenticated data outlives logout; stale content can be served after deploy.
- User / business impact: privacy exposure and stale-data confusion — only if the SW is ever registered.
- Security / privacy / reliability impact: tenant data cached client-side; no purge path.
- Recommended fix: rewrite the fetch handler to allowlist static assets, bypass `/api/` and non-GET, respect `no-store`, precache an offline HTML route, purge user-scoped caches on logout, and serve `/sw.js` with `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
- Suggested validation: unit tests over the fetch router with mocked `caches`/`fetch`; E2E asserting no `/api/v1/*` entries in Cache Storage.
- Owner suggestion: `@web` + security reviewer
- Effort estimate: M
- Dependencies: MOB-P2-001 decision.
- Status: open
- Note: new finding at 8d299b8d; the domain prompt's "service worker cache risks" special check.
